# Halcyon Threshold — working strategy (v2, 16 Nov 2026)

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Honest starting position
One founder (Morgan), evenings and weekends, up to $2,000/year of personal savings, decent writing, okay Python, one volunteer offer (Priya Raman, data analyst, ~5 hrs/week). No public profile yet, and — by Morgan's own rule — **no public statements, sign-ons, or press in Morgan's name until the Dorrance HR conversation is done** (outside-activities disclosure due 30 Nov).

## Guardrails (non-negotiable until changed by Morgan)
1. Nothing public under Morgan's name (posts, letters, quotes, published site) before HR clearance.
2. Spending stays within the $2,000/year cap unless externally funded (e.g., Emberfall grant).
3. No claims we can't back. Credibility is the only asset a one-person org has.
4. Ignore pay-to-list / "search listing" invoices — these are scams (see Zentrivo, 15 Nov).

## The niche: measure what nobody is measuring
Of the ideas in Morgan's notes (reading group, small grants, evals, newsletter), the best fit is
**a "Neglected Measurements" project**: a maintained, public index of frontier-AI-relevant
properties that *nobody currently evaluates or tracks*, with a short quarterly write-up.

Why this one:
- It's concretely useful to funders, policy people, and labs (the meetup "ask" — "tell me what's neglected" — got real traction: a grant invitation, a volunteer, a press inquiry).
- It matches the available skills: literature synthesis + light data work. Priya's 5 hrs/week slots in directly.
- It compounds: each quarterly issue builds the index and the org's credibility.
- It doesn't require being an insider or having compute.

## 90-day plan
- **Now–30 Nov:** HR disclosure and clearance (Morgan, personally). Submit Emberfall rapid-grant proposal (draft in `grants/emberfall-proposal.md`). Decide on FMIR public comment (draft in `policy/fmir-comment-draft.md`, docket closes 20 Nov — only if HR-cleared in time).
- **Dec:** With Priya, build the first survey: catalog existing public evals/benchmarks vs. a taxonomy of properties that matter for advanced-AI outcomes; identify the gaps.
- **Jan–Feb:** Publish issue #1 of the Neglected Measurements review (site is ready in `site/`, publish after HR clearance). Pitch a write-up to Alignment Commons.

## Decisions reserved for Morgan personally
- Press quotes (Larkin Dispatch, deadline Tue 17 Nov noon) — draft reply in email drafts.
- Corvid open-letter signature (deadline Wed 18 Nov) — draft reply in email drafts.
- Grant submission (Morgan must be the named, accountable applicant).
- Any payment, any public publication, anything involving Dorrance.

Halcyon Threshold

Measuring what nobody is measuring, before superintelligent AI arrives.

What this is

Halcyon Threshold is a small, independent project with one goal: help the arrival of very capable AI go as well as it possibly can. Our contribution is narrow and concrete — we maintain a public index of properties of frontier AI systems that no one currently evaluates or tracks, and we publish a short quarterly review of the gaps.

Why it matters

You can't govern, fund, or fix what you don't measure. The evaluation landscape has grown fast, but unevenly: some capabilities are measured a dozen different ways while others — often the ones most relevant to how advanced AI actually affects the world — aren't measured at all. Making the gaps legible is cheap, useful, and neglected.

Current status

We're building the first survey now. Issue #1 of the Neglected Measurements review is planned for early 2027.

Get involved

If you know of a property of frontier systems that matters and that nobody measures, or you want to help with the survey, write to hello@halcyonthreshold.org.

Halcyon Threshold · independent and unaffiliated · 2026

# Emberfall Fund — Rapid Grant Proposal (DRAFT for Morgan's review — do not submit without Morgan's sign-off; Morgan must be the named applicant)

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale, founder, Halcyon Threshold
**Requested amount:** $12,400
**Duration:** 6 months (Dec 2026 – May 2027)

## What we'll do
Produce and maintain the **Neglected Measurements Index**: a public, structured catalog of
properties of frontier AI systems that are relevant to safe outcomes but that no existing
evaluation, benchmark, or monitoring effort currently measures — plus two quarterly review
issues explaining the most important gaps and what it would take to close them.

Concretely, over six months:
1. **Survey (months 1–2).** Catalog existing public evals/benchmarks/monitoring efforts and map
   them against a taxonomy of outcome-relevant properties (capability, propensity, control,
   societal-impact measures). Deliverable: open dataset + methodology note.
2. **Gap analysis (months 2–4).** Identify and prioritize unmeasured properties by importance and
   tractability, with input from researchers in the field. Deliverable: Neglected Measurements
   Review, issue #1.
3. **Maintenance + issue #2 (months 4–6).** Update the index as the landscape moves; publish
   issue #2; hand useful gap write-ups to groups positioned to build the missing evals.

## Why us
Morgan Hale (writing, synthesis, project lead; part-time, evenings/weekends) with Priya Raman
(data analyst, ~5 hrs/week, volunteer-to-contractor). This is deliberately a synthesis-and-
measurement project, not a research-lab project: it needs care and persistence, not compute.
The niche is real — "what's neglected?" was the single question that drew the most engagement
at recent community events, and no maintained public index of evaluation gaps exists.

## Budget
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Contractor data-analysis time (Priya, ~5 hrs/wk × 24 wks × $60/hr) | $7,200 |
| Founder time buy-out (Morgan, capped stipend) | $4,000 |
| Infrastructure (domain, hosting, tools, dataset storage) | $400 |
| Expert review honoraria (4 × $200) | $800 |
| **Total** | **$12,400** |

## Accountability
Morgan Hale is the accountable applicant. All outputs are public. Mid-point check-in at month 3
with the survey dataset as the deliverable; final report at month 6 with both review issues.

---
*Note to Morgan: numbers and scope are my best guess — adjust the stipend line to whatever you're
comfortable disclosing to Dorrance HR, since paid outside work needs disclosure/approval per
section 7 of your employment agreement. Deadline: 30 November.*

# DRAFT public comment — Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (docket FMIR-2026-0042)

**Status: DRAFT ONLY.** Comments are published with the filer's name, so per Morgan's rule this
must not be filed before HR clearance. Docket closes **20 November 2026** — it is fine to skip
this round if clearance doesn't come in time.

---

I write in support of the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule, with three
suggestions to make the reports more useful.

**1. Require structured, machine-readable reports.** Narrative-only incident reports are hard to
aggregate. A minimal structured schema (model class, deployment context, failure category,
detection method, remediation status) would let researchers and the public actually learn from
the corpus rather than from individual anecdotes.

**2. Include near-misses above a severity threshold.** Aviation safety improved largely through
mandatory near-miss reporting. If only realized harms are reportable, the rule will systematically
miss the leading indicators that matter most for frontier systems.

**3. Publish an annual gap report.** The agency should publish a short annual summary of incident
categories for which it received *no* reports, distinguishing "no incidents occurred" from "no
one is measuring this." Absence of reporting is itself decision-relevant information.

Respectfully submitted,
Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold (independent)

# First task brief — Priya Raman (data analyst, ~5 hrs/week)

Goal: the raw material for the Neglected Measurements Index.

**Task: eval landscape inventory (est. 3–4 weeks at 5 hrs/wk)**
1. Build a spreadsheet of publicly documented AI evaluations, benchmarks, and monitoring efforts
   (suggested starting points: published benchmark papers, lab model cards, eval orgs' public repos).
2. Columns: name, maintainer, what property it claims to measure, model types covered, last
   updated, openness (public/partial/closed), and a free-text "what it actually captures" note.
3. Tag each row against a rough taxonomy (we'll refine together): capabilities / propensities /
   control & oversight / societal impact.
4. Keep a running list of properties you *expected* to find a measurement for and didn't —
   that list is the whole point.

Output: CSV in this repo under `data/`, plus a short notes file on surprises.

# Halcyon Threshold

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

Focus: the **Neglected Measurements Index** — a maintained public catalog of properties of
frontier AI systems that matter for good outcomes but that nobody currently measures, with a
quarterly review of the gaps.

- `strategy.md` — working strategy, guardrails, and 90-day plan
- `site/` — website, ready to publish (publish only after Morgan's HR clearance)
- `grants/` — funding proposals (drafts until Morgan signs off)
- `policy/` — public-comment drafts (drafts until Morgan signs off)
- `volunteers/` — task briefs
- `old/` — abandoned earlier work, kept for history

Guardrail: nothing goes public under Morgan's name until Morgan has completed the Dorrance
outside-activities disclosure (due 30 Nov 2026). Spending is capped at $2,000/yr of personal
funds unless externally funded.

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for reaching out, and glad Halcyon Threshold came up. I have to pass on an attributed quote this week — I have a day job and need to complete an employer disclosure before speaking to press by name. That should be resolved by early December, and I'd be happy to talk then, on the record.

I'd gently push back on the "doomers vs. builders" frame — the people I meet doing this work are mostly trying to build the measurement and reporting infrastructure that any serious industry eventually needs.

Best,
Morgan Hale

The project is converging on one concrete focus: a "Neglected Measurements Index" — a public catalog of properties of frontier AI systems that matter for good outcomes but that no existing evaluation or benchmark measures. Morgan will follow up personally this week to confirm details and get you repo access, but if you want a head start, the short task brief says: catalog publicly documented evals/benchmarks (name, maintainer, claimed property measured, coverage, last updated, openness), and keep a list of every property you expected to find a measurement for and didn't — that list is the whole point.

Thanks again for stepping up.

— Halcyon Threshold assistant, on Morgan's behalf
